title.analysis: Authentic title "FINANCIAL SYSTEM Explained in 50 Mins" capitalises the topic noun and makes an explicit time-cost promise. The actual duration is 3159 s (52.65 min), so the title understates it by 2.65 min (5.3%). The transcript delivers a breadth survey from coins to CBDCs, so "explained" means a survey, not depth. The five nearest peers use personal-outcome or threat hooks (WW3 ordering, passive-income milestone, a money trick, minimalist rules); this is the only institutional-explainer framing and sits at a TYPICAL 0.77455 ratio. Association only; no CTR or experiment evidence.

script.opening_words: You've got $847 in your checking account. Somewhere across town, a hedge fund manager just earned that in the time it took you to read this sentence. Somewhere else, a government just created $100 billion by typing numbers into a computer. And in a glass tower in lower Manhattan, 23-year-olds in suits are structuring deals that will determine whether entire companies live or die while charging fees that would make your mortgage look modest. None of them learned
script.ending_words: an inverted yield curve means for your mortgage rate. You know how 3 cents nearly ended global credit markets. And in a system this large, this powerful, and this deliberately confusing, that knowledge is not a small thing. That's the financial system. All of it. In one video. If this helped, subscribe. And if you made it this far, you genuinely know more about how money works than most people with finance degrees.
script.analysis: Full 45453 canonical characters read. Encyclopedic 14-segment survey ordered from barter to CBDCs. Recurring re-hooks ("Here's the number that should stop you cold", used twice), analogies (thermostat, supertanker, chef vs slow cooker, parallel city, email post office, Jenga) and scandal stories (Facebook IPO, 1MDB, Big Short, GameStop, Toys R Us, 2008) carry the content. The closing turns populist ("not neutral... designed for the people who designed it") with a personal-relevance payoff. Verified: zero reserve requirements from 26 Mar 2020, the 5.25-5.5% target, FDIC $250K, the accredited-investor thresholds, SVB losing over $40B, and FSB NBFI $256.8T. Errors: Buffett-bet figures are interim, not final (index 8.5%); NBFI half-share misdated to the mid-2000s; CPI peak understated (9.1%); UK episode misdated; Benchmark 855x stated as 750x; the Sarah projection matches neither stated return; the 10% reserve example mislabels deposits as lending; Toys R Us interest unit missing. One sentence about Ivy League managers losing to index funds appears twice verbatim (a script reuse artifact). Most figures are unsourced in the video.
beat_map: Cold open: $847 balance vs hedge-fund pay, $100B typed money; promise to explain the entire system in one video.
Money origins: barter, commodity money, Lydian coins, paper money, Nixon 1971, fiat, 8% cash claim, CBDC teaser.
Central banks: three levers (rates, QE/QT, lender of last resort); COVID response; 2022 inflation; thermostat and supertanker analogies.
Commercial banks: fractional reserve to zero reserves, loans create deposits, net interest margin, FDIC, SVB 2023 run.
Investment banks: IPOs (Facebook 2012), M&A, capital raising; 1MDB scandal payload.
Stocks: Buttonwood, exchanges and indices, long-run returns via Sarah persona, 2020 volatility, ownership inequality, best-days lesson.
Bonds: 2022 losses, market size, price-yield inverse with lease analogy, yield-curve inversion, Carville quote.
Hedge funds: accreditation, leverage, 2-and-20, Buffett bet, Medallion, Big Short, GameStop.
Private equity vs venture capital: LBO debt mechanics, Toys R Us, power law, Thiel/Sequoia/Benchmark returns.
Mutual funds/ETFs/index funds: SPIVA underperformance, chef analogy, Bogle 1976, fee-gap math, passive overtaking active.
Insurance float and pensions: Berkshire float; DB to DC shift; retirement gap; UK 2022 LDI episode.
Shadow banking and plumbing: NBFI size, money-fund break of the buck 2008, repo spike 2019.
2008 crisis in six steps, then accountability anger.
CBDCs and mBridge; whole-system loop; derivatives notional; Jenga; leverage+interconnection+trigger; Dodd-Frank; personal relevance; populist close; subscribe CTA.

topic.analysis: Macro-financial system literacy: money, central banking, commercial and investment banks, equities, bonds, hedge funds, PE/VC, funds, insurance, pensions, shadow banking, 2008 and CBDCs, framed as one interconnected credit and leverage system that touches the viewer's mortgage and retirement.
topic.audience_problem: Viewers lacking a mental map of how financial institutions connect to their own borrowing, saving and retirement outcomes.
topic.time_sensitivity: Level figures (Fed balance sheet, FSB 2024 NBFI, CBDC counts, Meta revenue, Berkshire float) are date-bound to about early 2026; mechanisms are evergreen.
topic.narrative_angle: Close-the-knowledge-gap chronology from coins to CBDCs, scandal stories as payloads, and a populist "system not designed for you" close.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Test an original chaptered financial-system map: every figure date-stamped and sourced on screen, verified mechanics (reserve requirements, deposit insurance, accredited-investor rules) separated from contested statistics, plus a personal-relevance chapter, against a personal-outcome framed version.
topic.competition: Same-channel nearest-age peers in K01; not an independent niche or causal test

virality.analysis: Frozen 12269 views / 191.149 days = 64.18553 views/day. Against 10 peers 0.77455x (TYPICAL); against 5 peers 0.55674x (TYPICAL). Duration 3159 s is 2.40x the 10-peer median of 1316 s and the longest in the cohort. Engagement: 31.87 likes and 6.19 comments per 1,000 views (descriptive). The breadth-survey promise and the institutional framing are plausible but unestablished mechanisms; source correctness and reach are separate questions.
